title: Banana Bread
subtitle: Moist quick bread made with very ripe bananas
excerpt: Overripe bananas mashed into a tender, lightly spiced loaf with a sugary crust. The darker the bananas, the sweeter and more intensely flavoured the bread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Banana bread is a quick bread: it is leavened with baking powder and bicarbonate of soda rather than yeast, and does not require kneading. It originated in America during the 1930s when baking powder became widely available and home bakers were looking for uses for overripe fruit during the Depression. It reached Britain via American cookbooks and became popular post-war. The key to good banana bread is using bananas that are completely black and very soft: these have the highest sugar content and a strong flavour. Yellow or slightly speckled bananas produce a much blander loaf. Walnuts or chocolate chips are popular additions.

content.text: Do not overmix the batter after the flour goes in. A few streaks of flour are fine. Overmixing develops the gluten and produces a tough, dense loaf. The banana bread is done when a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. It darkens quickly on top because of the high sugar content; if it is browning too fast, lay a sheet of foil loosely over the tin.

items.preparation: very ripe, blackened; about 300 g peeled

content.text: Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin with baking parchment. In a large bowl, mash the bananas to a rough puree with a fork.

Whisk the melted butter, sugar, eggs, and vanilla into the bananas until combined. Fold in the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon, and salt. Add the milk and stir briefly until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour into the prepared tin and bake for 55 to 65 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack. Slice when cool.
